Package org.checkerframework.framework.type.visitor

Class EquivalentAtmComboScannerVisitedTest

java.lang.Object
org.checkerframework.framework.type.visitor.EquivalentAtmComboScannerVisitedTest
public class EquivalentAtmComboScannerVisitedTest extends Object
Unit tests for EquivalentAtmComboScanner.Visited, the recursion guard of EqualityAtmComparer (and so of AnnotatedTypeMirror.equals(java.lang.Object)) and of the poly collector.

Visited is an open-addressing table keyed on the identity of both types of a pair. The checker test suites exercise it only through type comparisons, which rarely record more than a few pairs, so these tests target its boundaries directly: identity (not equality) of the keys, colliding pairs and probes that wrap around the end of the table, growth across every threshold with every pair and result preserved, replacing a pair's result (including a null result, which contains distinguishes from an absent pair), and clearing a table of the initial size (in place) and a grown one (dropped). The last test compares the table against the nested IdentityHashMaps it replaced over a seeded sequence of operations.

Collisions are made deterministic without assuming anything about identity hash codes: a test creates fresh first types until EquivalentAtmComboScanner.Visited.slotFor(java.lang.Object[], java.lang.Object, java.lang.Object) maps a pair to the wanted home entry of an empty table of the relevant capacity, and then inspects the table to confirm where the entry landed. The home entry depends on the first type only, so pairs that share a first type collide by construction, which one test covers directly.
